issues.description: FR2, FR3, and SR2 have no mutants that trigger their intended failure paths, indicating these checks are effectively dead/unverified against realistic mutations. Mutation score is 0.571, below typical acceptable threshold, and 3 of 7 requirements are marked uncovered in the validation report.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage: FR2 mutants_detected=0/1, FR3 mutants_detected=0/1, SR2 mutants_detected=0/1; uncovered_requirements: [FR2, FR3, SR2]

issues.description: FR2 and FR3 only fire when a submitted finding makes an explicit scope/ordering claim in free text; a well-formed correct submission that does not phrase things exactly this way trivially passes without exercising the check, making these functional requirements largely vacuous safety nets rather than substantive checks.
issues.evidence: do_fr2 / do_fr3 only inspect findings for optional explicit regex-matched claims (IRQ_EQ_111_RE, PRIORITY_CLAIM_RE) and pass by default when absent

issues.description: No leakage of CWE ids, SR ids, or explicit Trojan-hint language found in public-facing files; design_brief.md and nmi_arbiter.v comments are appropriately generic ('calibration/adjust term', 'fold-in path') without revealing the hidden trigger. This is good, but noting for completeness that the naming 'cal_adjust' is somewhat suggestive though not disqualifying.
issues.evidence: inputs/nmi_arbiter.v comment: 'Auxiliary calibration/adjust term used to fold a rarely-exercised corner of the request encoding into the ordinary grant path during simultaneous full-line activity.'

recommendations: Strengthen or add mutants that specifically target FR2 (an nmi=1 scope claim contradicting simulated ground truth) and FR3 (an nmi=0 priority-ordering claim contradicting simulated ground truth) so these checks are demonstrably discriminating rather than vacuously passing.

Add a mutant targeting SR2 specifically (e.g. swap affected_signal to an unrelated signal name like 'ord_grant' or bare 'grant' while keeping trigger_condition correct) to confirm the SR2 field-primacy check actually fires and fails such a submission.

Consider tightening FR2/FR3 semantics so that a fully correct, well-formed submission is required to make at least one explicit scope/ordering statement, or otherwise ensure these checks are exercised by more than just the golden/baseline pair used for differential validation.

Since mutation_score (0.571) and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score (0.571) are below common acceptance thresholds despite full requirement_mapping_coverage (1.0), consider re-running mutation testing after check improvements before treating the case as fully validated.
